extracted.intended_audience: Users of the Magma computational algebra system (mathematicians and computational group theorists) performing group constructions and computations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reference for creating, manipulating, and analysing groups in Magma: covers group categories, constructors for abstract and concrete groups, element/subgroup/quotient operations, invariants, series, characteristic subgroups, conjugacy classes, and available algorithms/caveats. Intended as a handbook chapter for practical use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for element normal form (ENF) and structure normal form (SNF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most structural computation requires the category to possess an element normal form algorithm and, in addition, a structure normal form. A category possessing a structure normal form will be referred to as a SNF-category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of an ENF implies membership and equality of arbitrary subgroups can be determined. SNF additionally allows structure computations (e.g., uniform random sampling). Examples: polycyclic groups, abelian groups and permutation groups are SNF-categories. fp-groups are neither ENF nor SNF. Some matrix-group categories are SNF (matrix groups over finite fields and finite euclidean rings; finite matrix groups over fields and euclidean rings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of group categories (abstract vs concrete)
rubrics_metrics.description: Group categories may be classified into those defined by presentations (fp-groups, pc-groups and abelian groups) and those given in concrete representation (permutation groups and matrix groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminology: 'abstract groups' = defined by generators and relations; 'concrete groups' = subgroups of Sym(X) (permutation) or GL(n,R) (matrix). Semantics of some operators differ by category; consult relevant Handbook chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract group constructors and relation syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract groups can be constructed with FreeGroup(n), FreeAbelianGroup(n) and the constructors Group< x1,...,xi | relations >, AbelianGroup< ... >, PCGroup< ... > where relations are words in the generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each relation may be w1 = w2; w (meaning equals identity); or w1 = w2 = ... = wk. If using PCGroup constructor, relations must define a polycyclic group. Examples provided for FreeAbelianGroup(5), p6<s,t> := Group<s,t | s^3 = t^2 = (s*t)^6 = 1> and AbelianGroup<a,b | a+2*b=0>.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete group constructors and generator representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete groups: Sym(n) or Sym(T) for symmetric groups; GeneralLinearGroup(n,R) (GL(n,R)) for matrix groups; constructors PermutationGroup< n | generators >, PermutationGroup< T | generators >, MatrixGroup< n, R | generators >.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permutation generators may be sequences or cycle products; matrix generators may be length-n^2 sequences of ring elements. Generator lists may include elements of related structures, sets/sequences, or subgroups (contributing their generators).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer built-in standard group functions when available
rubrics_metrics.description: Some frequently needed groups are built into Magma (CyclicGroup, DihedralGroup, AbelianGroup, AlternatingGroup, SymmetricGroup, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the dedicated function (e.g., AlternatingGroup(GrpPerm,9)) rather than building via sub< Sym(9) | ... > because Magma constructs the group quickly and knows additional information such as order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generator assignment names and printnames
rubrics_metrics.description: Generators from standard groups may be given special names by a generator assignment statement. These names become identifiers and in GrpAb, GrpFP and GrpPC they also become printnames for the generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: D5<rot,refl> := DihedralGroup(GrpFP,5) to help geometric intuition by naming rotation/reflection generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic operators on group elements (multiplicative and additive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables of arithmetic notation: multiplicative groups use x*y, x^-1, x^n, x^y (conjugate), x/y, (x,y) (commutator), (x1,...,xn) (left-normed commutator), Id(G). Additive groups use x+y, -x, n*x, x-y, Id(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: for categories without an ENF (fp-groups), elements returned will not be canonical. Examples demonstrate conjugation, commutator calculations and the use of Id(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Boolean operators and equality semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Boolean operators: x eq y (true if equal), x ne y, x cmpeq y (compatible and equal), IsIdentity(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In fp-groups, elements x and y are equal iff they reduce to the same word under free reduction. Use equality carefully in categories without ENF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of an element (Order(x))
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is an element of finite order in an ENF-group G, Order(x) will return that order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order(x) depends on ENF availability; for ENF-categories it works; otherwise behaviour may be limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random element generation with SNF vs without
rubrics_metrics.description: If a SNF has been constructed for G, Random(G) returns elements sampled with equal probability. If no SNF exists, Random(G) simply evaluates a short random word in the generators and is usually far from uniform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative approach without SNF: RandomProcess(G) builds an expanded generating set X and returns a process P; Random(P) gives a new element at cost of one multiplication and mutates X. Control randomness via parameters Slots (size of X) and Scramble (number of multiplications to construct X).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgroup constructor sub< G | generators > semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: The subgroup H generated by a set S may be defined using sub< G | generators >. The generator list items may be elements, sequences defining elements, sets/sequences of elements, subgroups (contributing their generators), or sets/sequences of subgroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The constructor returns two values: the subgroup H (same category as G) and a monomorphism φ: H → G giving the embedding. Example: M2<s,t>, f := sub<U2 | r1*r2, r1*r3>.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normal closure constructor (ncl-constructor)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ncl-constructor creates the smallest normal subgroup of G containing the designated subset S (treats S as normal generators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It has the same argument rules as sub. Use ncl when normality is required; sub constructs the subgroup closure instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard subgroup construction functions and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma provides many functions for standard subgroups (conjugate H^g, intersection H meet K, Centralizer(G,x), Centralizer(G,H), Core(G,H), Normalizer(G,H), H^G (normal closure), pCore(G,p), SylowSubgroup(G,p), etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very subtle and efficient algorithms are used. Availability varies by category; e.g., Centralizer, pCore and SylowSubgroup are not applicable to fp-groups. To remember argument order, the group in which the subgroup is calculated is typically the first argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient constructor quo< G | generators > semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Given subset S and normal closure N, quo< G | generators > creates the quotient group Q = G/N and returns Q and the natural surjection τ: G → Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In current version, quotient Q is returned in same category as G except when G is a matrix group (then Q is returned as a permutation group). Future versions may return quotients in a new category. Example: Q, f := quo< S4 | (1,2)(3,4), (1,3)(2,4) >.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special quotient functions and their outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Special quotient algorithms exist: AbelianQuotient(G) (G/[G,G]), pQuotient(G,p,c), SolubleQuotient(G), RadicalQuotient(G) (quotient by soluble radical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each returns the quotient Q and the natural surjection τ: G → Q. Availability varies by category. pQuotient example shows progress messages when Print parameter is set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order and FactoredOrder for groups and Todd–Coxeter caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Order(G) returns the group's order as an integer; FactoredOrder(G) returns factorization. For fp-groups, Order uses the Todd–Coxeter procedure to enumerate cosets and may fail or exhaust memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Todd–Coxeter is used with a default limit of one million cosets; the user may override by calling Todd–Coxeter directly. Exponent(G) computes exponent only for groups with a computable SNF. For infinite matrix groups, Order will fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index and FactoredIndex restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Index(G,H) and FactoredIndex(G,H) return the index [G:H] as integer or factorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions may only be applied to matrix groups for which a BSGS can be computed (practically, finite matrix groups defined over a field or a euclidean ring).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests of group properties and fp-group applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions such as IsAbelian, IsNilpotent, IsCyclic, IsSpecial, IsSoluble(IsSolvable), IsElementaryAbelian, IsPerfect, IsSimple, IsExtraSpecial determine abstract properties of a group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With the exception of IsPerfect, these functions are not applicable to fp-groups. Use the appropriate functions only in categories with the needed computational infrastructure (typically SNF).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests on subgroup embedding properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions test embedding properties: IsConjugate(G,H,K), IsSubnormal(G,H), IsCentral(G,H), IsNormal(G,H), IsSelfNormalizing(G,H), IsMaximal(G,H).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions determine how subgroups H (and K) are embedded in G; applicability may vary by category and depending on whether ENF/SNF are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic subgroup functions and SNF/p-group exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions for characteristic subgroups include Centre(G), Hypercentre(G), DerivedSubgroup(G), FittingSubgroup(G), FrattiniSubgroup(G), Radical(G), SolubleResidual(G), Agemo(G,i), Omega(G,i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All but one of these functions require a SNF for G; the exception is DerivedSubgroup which may be applied to an fp-group. Agemo and Omega are defined only for p-groups; FrattiniSubgroup is implemented only for p-groups. Availability of functions may differ across categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series functions and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions to produce series: ChiefSeries, CompositionSeries, ElementaryAbelianSeries, DerivedSeries, DerivedLength, JenningsSeries, LowerCentralSeries, NilpotencyClass, pCentralSeries(G,p), SubnormalSeries(G,H), UpperCentralSeries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These series functions apply only to groups for which a SNF can be computed (not available for fp-groups). Some series require p-group or soluble-group hypotheses. Use appropriate series for structural analysis (derived vs lower central gives solubility vs nilpotency info).

rubrics_metrics.name: CompositionFactors(G) output format and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: CompositionFactors(G) (for permutation and matrix groups) returns sequence of tuples F1,...,Fr identifying composition factors Si = Ti/Ti-1. Each tuple Fi = <fi, di, qi> identifies family of simple groups and parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation of fi, di, qi follows Table 29.11; sporadic groups mapping in Table 29.12. If G is simple, NameSimple(G) returns an identifying tuple. The order corresponds to some composition series; the tuples give the isomorphism type of each composition factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugacy class problems and main operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Three major issues: determine whether two elements are conjugate in G; determine the classes of G (representative and invariants for each class); determine quickly the class containing a given element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IsConjugate(G,x,y) tests conjugacy and returns a conjugating element g if they are conjugate. Class(H,x) / Conjugates(H,x) gives the set of conjugates under H (do not use to enumerate large classes). For class size, use Index(G, Centralizer(G,x)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing all conjugacy classes (ConjugacyClasses / Classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classes(G) returns a sequence of tuples for each conjugacy class: (order of elements in class, length of class, representative element).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sequence can be indexed; printing has a special display format. Determination of classes is computationally hard; several algorithms are available and may be selected with an Al parameter to Classes (values: "Action", "Random", "Extension"). Choose algorithm based on group size and structure: "Action" computes orbits (good for small groups), "Random" attempts to find an element in each class, "Extension" uses inductive algorithm via quotients determined by an elementary abelian series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency notes and algorithm selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Some operations have more efficient Magma functions or alternative algorithms that should be preferred in practice (e.g., Class(G,x) vs ClassMap, dedicated subgroup/quotient algorithms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: computing conjugacy class by brute-force conjugation is less efficient than Class(G,x) or ClassMap when handling many elements; use dedicated functions (e.g., AlternatingGroup) when available for speed and extra information. Many functions are unavailable or inefficient in fp-groups; prefer SNF-capable categories for heavy structural computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation changes in certain outputs (matrix quotient -> permutation group)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the current version of Magma, quotients of matrix groups are returned as permutation groups rather than matrix groups; future versions may change this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of returned category type when programming (e.g., Q returned by quo< MatrixGroup | ... > may be a permutation group). Check Handbook/online help for up-to-date behaviour.
